q: Chemical energy of $5.0\,\text{kJ}$ is released from the battery of a toy car, and the car gains kinetic energy of $1.2\,\text{kJ}$. What does the rest of the energy change into, and how much of it is there?
a: Into thermal energy, because energy is conserved: $E_\text{thermal} = E_\text{initial} - E_\text{k} = 5.0\,\text{kJ} - 1.2\,\text{kJ} = 3.8\,\text{kJ}$.

q: On an electricity bill you pay for the "used" electrical energy. Why can energy still not be used up?
a: Energy does not disappear but changes into another form: a device changes electrical energy into, for example, light, motion and thermal energy. The bill is for the fact that easily usable electrical energy is changed into other forms, finally into thermal energy that spreads into the surroundings.
